Name: Electoral Democracy Index
What it measures: Free and fair elections, suffrage, freedom of expression and association, elected officials.
Teaching notes: The baseline is it a democracy measure. Hungary and Poland trajectories since 2010 are classic teaching charts.

Name: Liberal Democracy Index
What it measures: Electoral democracy plus rule of law, judicial and legislative constraints on the executive.
Teaching notes: Best single measure for backsliding; the drop is steeper here than on polyarchy, which shows backsliding hits liberal components first.

Name: Participatory Democracy Index
What it measures: Electoral democracy plus civil society participation, direct democracy, local and regional government.
Teaching notes: Measures citizen power beyond periodic balloting.

Name: Deliberative Democracy Index
What it measures: Electoral democracy plus reasoned public justification and respect for counterarguments.
Teaching notes: Pairs well with polarization debates and public discourse quality.

Name: Egalitarian Democracy Index
What it measures: Electoral democracy plus equal protection of rights and equal access to power and resources.
Teaching notes: Evaluates socio-economic equality as a democratic pillar.

Name: Regimes of the World
What it measures: Closed autocracy (0), electoral autocracy (1), electoral democracy (2), liberal democracy (3).
Teaching notes: Hungary has been classified as an electoral autocracy since 2018 - a powerful discussion starter.

Name: Regimes of the World with ambiguous categories
What it measures: Adds upper and lower bound categories for cases near thresholds.
Teaching notes: Shows uncertainty near thresholds; useful for Serbia, Georgia, Turkiye.

Name: Liberal Component Index
What it measures: Rule of law plus judicial and legislative constraints on the executive.
Teaching notes: Isolates the liberal pillar from elections.

Name: Judicial Constraints on Executive Index
What it measures: Executive respects constitution and complies with courts; judicial independence.
Teaching notes: Direct link to EU rule-of-law conditionality and Polish judicial reforms.

Name: Legislative Constraints on Executive Index
What it measures: Legislature questions, investigates and oversees the executive.
Teaching notes: Checks whether parliament can hold executive accountable.

Name: Rule of Law Index
What it measures: Laws transparent, independently and predictably enforced; impartial administration.
Teaching notes: Compare with EU Justice Scoreboard.

Name: Freedom of Expression Index
What it measures: Media freedom, freedom of discussion, academic and cultural expression.
Teaching notes: Media capture in Hungary and Serbia.

Name: Freedom of Association Index (thick)
What it measures: Parties and civil society organizations can form and operate freely.
Teaching notes: Examines multi-party competition and civic assembly.

Name: Clean Elections Index
What it measures: Free and fair elections: no fraud, intimidation, or vote buying; autonomous election body.
Teaching notes: Elections often stay relatively clean while liberal components erode - a key backsliding pattern.

Name: Civil Society Participation Index
What it measures: Civil society consulted and involved in policymaking.
Teaching notes: Measures grassroots engagement in public policy.

Name: Academic Freedom Index
What it measures: Freedom to research and teach, institutional autonomy, campus integrity.
Teaching notes: The CEU expulsion from Budapest is a vivid case.

Name: Women Political Empowerment Index
What it measures: Womens civil liberties, civil society participation and political participation.
Teaching notes: Essential metric for gender equity in governance.

Name: Political Corruption Index
What it measures: Executive, legislative, judicial and public-sector corruption.
Teaching notes: Reverse direction from other indices; flag in the tool.

Name: Neopatrimonial Rule Index
What it measures: Clientelism, presidentialism and regime corruption.
Teaching notes: Reverse direction; useful for comparative authoritarianism.

Name: Government Media Censorship Effort
What it measures: Does government attempt to censor print or broadcast media?
Teaching notes: Direct measure of government media suppression.

Name: Harassment of Journalists
What it measures: Are journalists harassed by government or powerful actors?
Teaching notes: Higher score indicates greater safety and freedom for journalists.

Name: Media Bias
What it measures: Is there media coverage of the opposition?
Teaching notes: Crucial indicator for electoral level playing field.

Name: CSO Repression
What it measures: Does government attempt to repress civil society organizations?
Teaching notes: Hungary foreign agents style NGO law (2017) shows up here.

Name: High Court Independence
What it measures: When the high court rules on important cases, does it reflect government wishes?
Teaching notes: Polands Constitutional Tribunal crisis after 2015.

Name: Lower Court Independence
What it measures: Lower court independence from executive influence.
Teaching notes: Measures everyday justice system independence.

Name: Compliance with Judiciary
What it measures: Does government comply with important court decisions it disagrees with?
Teaching notes: Key test for executive overreach.

Name: Executive Respects Constitution
What it measures: Do members of executive respect constitution?
Teaching notes: Core indicator of constitutionalism.

Name: Election Free and Fair
What it measures: Overall judgment of how free and fair the last national election was.
Scale / direction: Model estimate ~ -5 to +5 (higher = more free & fair)
Teaching notes: Direct assessment of national election integrity.

Name: Election Government Intimidation
What it measures: Was opposition harassed or intimidated by government during election?
Teaching notes: Higher score indicates fair and intimidation-free campaigns.

Name: Political Polarization
What it measures: Is society polarized into antagonistic political camps?
Teaching notes: Reverse direction: higher scores indicate deeper political hostility and social divide.
